reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 4

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency asks students to ILLUSTRATE division via number-line jumps and via its multiplication-inverse relationship, but the samples are plain quotient-computation questions ('What is 670÷10?', '300÷5=___') with no number-line reference in the text and no explicit multiplication-inverse framing (e.g. '6×7=42, so 42÷7=?').

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: variant_registry lists 20 combos for division, but none of the 5 samples given demonstrate the number-line or inverse-multiplication illustration this competency specifically names; a visual/model component may exist outside the text field though.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The quotient questions are short single-step computations appropriate for grade 3 quarter 4 reading level.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Both mcq and cloze formats appear, but no sample text links a division fact back to its multiplication counterpart, which the competency requires students to connect.

competency_alignment.rationale: Plain quotient computation is a reasonable building block but doesn't by itself demonstrate the 'illustrate...as inverse of multiplication' concept this specific competency emphasizes over q4_1's plain fact fluency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividend/divisor magnitudes (30-670 divided by single/double-digit numbers) are a reasonable early-Q4 range for grade 3 division.
